    Trail SnacksJunkyard sandwichesButtered white bread with mustard, ham, cheddar and pickles, wrapped to goHow to make it8 slices of white bread30g butter, soft2 tbsp yellow mustard200g leg ham100g cheddar, sliced8 dill pickle slicesButter the bread and spread with mustard.Fill with ham, cheddar and pickles.Cut in half and wrap each tightly in baking paper.Trail walk devilled eggsDevilled eggs with mustard and paprika, packed for the walk along the tracksHow to make it8 eggs4 tbsp whole egg mayonnaise2 tsp yellow mustard1 tsp white vinegar1 tsp sweet paprika1 bunch chivesLower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes.Cool them in iced water, then peel.Halve the eggs lengthways and tip the yolks into a bowl.Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth.Spoon the filling back into the whites and dust with paprika and snipped chives.Peanut butter and jelly on whiteWrapped for a two day walk on the tracks.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Mess Hall MainsCampfire hamburger pattiesThick beef patties on white bread with soft fried onions and tomato sauceHow to make it800g beef mince1 tsp salt1/2 tsp pepper2 onions, sliced8 slices of white bread4 tbsp tomato sauce1 tbsp vegetable oilSeason the mince and shape into thick patties.Fry the onions in oil until soft and sweet.Cook the patties over hot coals or in a smoking pan until cooked through, turning once.Serve between thick slices of white bread with the onions and tomato sauce.Pan-charred franks with onion relishSmoky sausages blackened in a skillet, soft buns, jammy onion, mustard and picklesHow to make itNot on tonight's cookSmoky franks charred in a hot pan, tucked into soft buns with sticky onion relish, mustard and crunchy pickles.Slice 3 onions thinly and cook in 30g butter over low heat for 25 minutes until jammy, then add 1 tbsp brown sugar and 2 tbsp cider vinegar and cook 2 minutes more.Score 8 franks and cook in a hot cast iron pan for 6 minutes, turning, until blistered.Warm 8 hot dog buns in the pan.Fill each bun with a frank, a spoon of onion relish, mustard and sliced pickles.Campfire TreatsBlueberry pieLattice topped blueberry pie, cooled before slicingHow to make it750g blueberries150g caster sugar1 lemon, juiced3 tbsp cornflour4 sheets of sweet shortcrust pastryToss the blueberries with sugar, lemon juice and cornflour.Line a pie dish with two pastry sheets and fill.Cut the remaining sheets into strips and weave a lattice on top.Bake at 190°C until deep golden and bubbling.Cool completely before cutting, at least 3 hours.Campfire marshmallowsToasted marshmallows dipped in dark chocolate, squashed between digestive biscuitsHow to make it16 marshmallows100g dark chocolate, melted32 digestive biscuitsMelt the chocolate in a bowl over hot water.Toast the marshmallows on sticks over the fire or a gas flame until blistered.Dip in the chocolate and squash between two biscuits. Eat while still gooey.Homemade cherry gummiesSoft chews of real cherry juice and gelatine in sour sugar, for the campfire Pez debateHow to make itNot on tonight's cookSoft cherry gummies made with real cherry juice and gelatine, rolled in sour sugar, the kind of lolly the boys argue about by the fire.Heat 250ml cherry juice with 80g caster sugar until dissolved.Sprinkle 30g powdered gelatine over 100ml cold cherry juice, leave 5 minutes, then stir into the hot juice until clear.Add 1 tbsp lemon juice and pour into a lightly oiled 20cm square tin.Chill 3 hours until firm.Cut into squares and roll in 50g caster sugar mixed with 1 tsp citric acid.Canteen DrinksCastle Rock sarsaparilla floatSarsaparilla poured over vanilla ice creamHow to make it1 L vanilla ice cream1.3 L sarsaparilla, coldChill four tall glasses in the freezer.Scoop the ice cream into each glass.Pour the sarsaparilla slowly down the side, let the foam settle, then top up.
